evidence.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight
Since there is no net external force on the aircraft, the aircraft maintains a constant airspeed as described by Newton’s First Law of Motion.
The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.
the distance flown is equal to the ground speed times the time aloft.
The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).

objectives: Calculate cruising distance from ground speed and time aloft using distance equals speed times time
Determine maximum range from ground speed and maximum flight time
Explain how fuel load limits time aloft and range
analysis.unsupportedReason: The source teaches constant-velocity aircraft range using d = V * t and R = V * tmax, which matches none of the listed activity engines.
